critical_code_review_comments: rc_media.py: excellent separation — DURABLE_URL_RE + blob:/data: rejection at the service boundary; only durable /api/{media,images,videos}/... or https://... URLs accepted, matching the established website_media.py pattern. Registry never stores files, only pointers.

activate_version() uses a two-step conditional update: first deactivate the (asset,theme,device) active row, then flip target status:{$ne:'active'}. Concurrent activations resolve to exactly one because the flip is conditional and returns 409 if lost. Correct.

build_manifest() 30s in-memory cache invalidated on every activation/reset/alt-change/branding-change. Fast for hub/dashboard/wizard reads. Note: single-process cache — behind multiple workers, each worker holds its own; 30s is short enough to not be a real issue for admin operations, and manifest is small.
reset_to_default preserves history — versions become 'deactivated', restore path via activate endpoint. Great UX + audit trail.
rc_media_alt uses $setOnInsert alongside $set — subtle but correct: on first insert it seeds active_version_id=null; on updates it only touches alt/updated_by/updated_at.

Branding PATCH validates each key individually with per-field max length (product_name 80/short 40/tagline 120) and coerces flags to bool; unknown keys 400 immediately (no partial writes accepted). before/after audit rows are per-changed-key, small and readable.

Center-branding endpoint properly gates on center_branding_enabled AND per-field flags (user_center_logo_allowed / user_center_cover_allowed). Not enabling the flag → 403, enabling but no upload flag → 403, enabling both → durable URL check → save. Good defence in depth.
Router ordering in responsibility_center.py: /preferences is defined BEFORE /{center_id} so it isn't shadowed by the dynamic segment. Verified by 200 responses for both GET and PATCH.
AdminRcMedia.jsx correctly uses rcApi + refreshRcManifest() on every mutating action so UI + hub stay in sync post-activation without a hard reload.

MINOR — build_manifest() cache is per-worker and doesn't share across replicas; combined with 30s TTL it's fine for admin cadence, but if the platform ever scales to many workers with heavy manifest traffic, consider a small Redis/memcached layer or push-based invalidation.
MINOR — activate_version() re-reads with find_one after update; could be avoided by returning the updated doc via find_one_and_update. Negligible.
